components.note: 亻 (person) plus 尔 (an old second-person pronoun) — combines to form 你, the modern word for 'you.'
宀 (roof) — 家 is about a home, the space under a roof.
豕 (shǐ, 'pig') supplies the ancient sound for 家; keeping a pig under one's roof was also a practical sign of a household in ancient China, though the modern readings jiā and shǐ no longer rhyme.
一 (a line, representing a target or standard) — 正 shows a foot arriving exactly at the right mark.
止 (foot, to stop) — arriving and stopping precisely at the target gives 正 its meaning of 'correct' or 'straight.'
⺷ (sheep, related to 羊) — 义 relates to what is right or moral, linked to the idea of sacrificial sheep used in rituals of righteousness.
乂 (yì) gives the sound — 义 is also pronounced yì, an exact match.
网 depicts a woven mesh net stretched over a frame — a picture of a fishing or hunting net, giving 网 its meaning 'net, network.'
立 (to stand) — 站 relates to standing, and by extension a stop or station where one stands to wait
占 (zhàn) gives the sound — 站 is also pronounced zhàn, an exact match

meanings: (after a noun) place where it is located

components.note: 户 (door) — 所 evokes a location or place, such as where a door stands.
斤 (axe) — combined with 户 (door), the image of an axe at a door gave rise to the abstract sense of 'a place' or 'that which.'
土 (earth/soil) — 在 originally related to standing on the ground
才 (cái) gives the sound — 在 is pronounced zài, a close match
彡 (shān) is the historical phonetic component of 参; sound change over time has left little resemblance to the modern reading cān
讠 (speech) — relates to 议's meaning 'to discuss, deliberate; opinion.'
义 (yì) gives the sound — 议 is also pronounced yì, an exact match.
贝 (shell/money — cowrie shells were historically used as currency) — 员 originally related to counting or officials responsible for accounts, later broadening to mean 'member' or 'personnel.'
凵 depicts an open container or pit, shown here holding something dangerous inside.
乂 is a crossed mark suggesting something tangled or harmful — trapped inside the container 凵, it gives 凶 its meaning 'vicious, ominous.'
口 (a vessel), shown four times — a set of cooking vessels.
犬 (a dog) — guarding the vessels, the source of 器's meaning 'vessel, tool, instrument.'
尺 (a ruler/measure) — represents rules or measures being set.
口 (mouth) — measures being discussed aloud in one place gave 局 its meaning 'bureau, office, situation.'
长 (simplified from 長) depicts an elderly figure with long flowing hair and a cane — length and seniority are linked in the original picture.
纟 (silk thread) originally related to spinning thread to completion, extended to mean accomplishment.
责 (duty) sits beside the thread element, tying the idea of one's responsibilities to what gets accomplished, giving 绩 its meaning 'achievement.'
弓 (bow) — a strong bow that took great force to draw gave 强 its meaning 'strong, powerful.'
虫 was a different phonetic element historically; its pronunciation has shifted so far from qiáng over time that the sound link is no longer obvious.
灬 (fire) — 烈 relates to something as intense and fierce as fire
列 (liè) gives the sound — an exact match with 烈's reading liè
心 (heart/mind) — 意 relates to thought, intention, and meaning, things of the mind.
音 (yīn) is the historical phonetic element; its modern reading has drifted from yì, though both share a similar vowel.
口 (mouth) — 味 relates to taste, sensed in the mouth.
未 (wèi) gives the sound — an exact match with 味.
壴 (a drum) — beating a drum in celebration
口 (mouth) — singing along in celebration
刂 (knife) contributes to the character's form, though its link to 剧's meaning 'drama' has faded over time.
居 (jū) gives a rhyme close to jù, with the tone shifted.
A short stroke placed below a longer one — the mirror image of 上 (up), together forming a simple, opposite pair.

meanings: to go to teach a class

components.note: A short stroke placed above a longer one — a simple graphic way to show 'up' or 'above,' contrasted with 下 (down), which flips the strokes.
讠 (speech) — 课 relates to lessons taught through spoken instruction.
果 (guǒ) gives a sound distantly related to kè, having drifted apart over time.
艹 (grass) forms the top of the character.
木 (tree), sheltered beneath a covering, together depict plants flourishing, giving 荣 its meaning 'glory, prosperity.'
言 (word, speech) at the bottom shows this relates to spoken reputation.
兴 (to prosper, flourish) above shows praise for success, giving 誉 its meaning 'reputation, praise.'
云 here stands in for an older form meaning "to speak of, to taste," 尝's core meaning.
尚 (shàng) gives a sound distantly related to cháng, having drifted apart over time.
云 here stands in for an older form meaning "to speak of, to taste," 尝's core meaning.
尚 (shàng) gives a sound distantly related to cháng, having drifted apart over time.
讠 (speech) — relates to 设's meaning 'to establish, set up,' something first proposed through words.
殳 (shū) served as the phonetic base; its pronunciation has since drifted well away from shè.
讠 (speech) — 计 relates to counting or planning through words and numbers.
十 (shí) gives a hint of the sound — 计 is pronounced jì, a connection that has shifted significantly over time.
帀 (a banner or covering) — flying above the scene.
刂 (a knife) — wielded with skill beneath the banner, an image of expertise giving 师 its meaning 'master, teacher, expert.'
辶 (to walk) — 违 involves stepping away from what is required, i.e. disobeying.
韦 (wéi) is an exact match for the sound of 违.
厂 (a cliff or overhang) — 反 pictures pushing against a steep surface.
又 (a hand) — a hand pushing back against a cliff gave 反 its meaning 'to turn over' or 'opposite.'
阝 (hill) — 阶 originally referred to steps built into a hillside or mound
介 (jiè) gives a sound close to 阶's reading jiē, sharing a similar historical pronunciation
段 shows 殳 (a hand wielding a tool) cutting or shaping stone into pieces — giving 段 its meaning 'section, segment, paragraph.'
不 (not) — 否 relates directly to negation and denial
口 (kǒu) gives a loose sound connection to 否's reading fǒu
讠 (speech) — 认 relates to recognizing or acknowledging something, often expressed through words.
人 (rén) gives the sound — 认 is pronounced rèn, a close variant of the same sound.
冏 (bright, a window admitting light) — appears in 商's ancient form, though its exact link to 'commerce, to discuss' is unclear today.
章 — a graphic element whose original contribution to the character's meaning has been lost over time.
里 (a unit of distance, related to a village measure) — 量 relates to measuring quantity.
旦 (dàn) gives a hint of the sound — 量 is pronounced liàng, a connection that has shifted significantly over time.
亻 (person) — 什 originally referred to a group of people.
十 (ten) — combined with 亻 (person), 什 originally described a group of ten; the character later came to be used for the common word 什么 (what).
屮 (a young sprout) growing up and out of 凵 (a container or pit) — a picture of something emerging, hence 'going out.'
立 (to stand) — 站 relates to standing, and by extension a stop or station where one stands to wait
占 (zhàn) gives the sound — 站 is also pronounced zhàn, an exact match
亻 (person) — the one settling somewhere.
主 (host, master) — the idea of a person settled in a place as if hosting it, giving 住 its meaning 'to live, reside, stay.'
The character traces the front view of an ox's head, with the top stroke and crossing lines representing its curved horns and ears.
亻 (person) on the left represents someone tending to something small.
子 (child) on the right depicts the small, young thing being watched over, giving 仔 its meaning of something small or young.
十 (here representing a weapon or armor) — 克 pictures overcoming an opponent.
兄 (a person, here representing a formidable figure) — overcoming a strong opponent gave 克 its meaning 'to overcome' or 'to be able to.'
禾 (a grain plant) — a sweet-smelling crop
日 — here standing in for sweetness (originally 甘), giving the sense of a pleasant smell
木 (tree) — 槟 names the areca palm and its nut.
宾 (bīn) gives an exact match for 槟's reading.
亻 (person) — 偷 describes a person's action, stealing.
俞 (yú) gives a sound distantly related to tōu, having drifted apart over time.
土 (here representing a person swinging their arms, not its usual meaning 'earth') — depicts someone in motion.
止 (a foot) — combined with the moving figure above, 走 shows a person walking or running.
艹 (grass/plant) — 艺 originally related to planting and cultivating skillfully
乙 (yǐ) gives a sound distantly related to 艺's reading yì, having drifted apart over time
宀 (roof) — 家 is about a home, the space under a roof.
豕 (shǐ, 'pig') supplies the ancient sound for 家; keeping a pig under one's roof was also a practical sign of a household in ancient China, though the modern readings jiā and shǐ no longer rhyme.
尸, here a variant of 厂, depicts a roof or shelter.
至 depicts arriving or coming to rest — settling under a roof gave 屋 its meaning 'house, room.'
田 (farmland) over 土 (earth/soil) — originally referred to a village or a measured unit of farmland, later extended to mean 'inside' or a unit of distance.
十 (here representing a weapon or armor) — 克 pictures overcoming an opponent.
兄 (a person, here representing a formidable figure) — overcoming a strong opponent gave 克 its meaning 'to overcome' or 'to be able to.'
艹 (grass) — 莱 names a weedy plant, goosefoot.
来 (lái) is an exact match for the sound of 莱.
扌 (hand) — relates to 技's meaning 'skill, technique,' a skill performed with the hands.
支 (zhī) served as the phonetic base; its pronunciation has since drifted well away from jì.
工 (work, tool) — 巧 relates to skill in craft or work.
丂 (kǎo) gives a sound close to qiǎo.
忄 (heart) — 情 relates to feelings and emotions.
青 (qīng) gives the sound — 情 is pronounced qíng, a close match differing only in tone.
咸 (all, together) — 感 relates to a shared reaction.
心 (heart) — feelings that stir the heart gave 感 its meaning 'to feel' or 'emotion.'
A vertical line 丨 running through the middle of a box or flag 口 — a simple image for the idea of 'center, middle.'
扌 (hand) — 提 relates to lifting or carrying something by hand.
是 (shì) gives a hint of the sound — 提 is pronounced tí, a connection that has shifted over time.
讠 (speech) — relates to 议's meaning 'to discuss, deliberate; opinion.'
义 (yì) gives the sound — 议 is also pronounced yì, an exact match.
辶 (to walk) — 逃 means to escape or flee, involving movement.
兆 (zhào) gives a rhyme close to táo, with the initial shifted.
辶 (to walk) — 避 means to avoid, moving away from something.
辟 (bì) gives the sound — an exact match with 避.
母 (mǔ, 'mother') serves as the phonetic base; the sound has since diverged from měi, so the connection is mostly historical today.
冂 depicts a boundary or border enclosing an area.
土 (earth/land) — the land enclosed within the border.
口 here depicts a well within that land — together giving 周 its early meaning of a bounded territory, and later 'circumference, week, the Zhou dynasty.'
罒 (a net) — the law closing in around wrongdoing
非 (wrong) — the wrongdoing itself, caught in the net
夕 (evening, night) — in the dark, one could not see a person's face, so calling out their name was necessary to identify them.
口 (mouth) — calling out with the mouth at night gave 名 its meaning 'name.'
行 (to go/walk) — 街 names a road where people walk and travel.
圭 (guī) gives a sound distantly related to jiē, having drifted apart over time.
匸 (an enclosure or boundary) — 区 pictures a defined territory.
乂 (a mark, here representing control or division) — dividing land into bounded territories gave 区 its meaning 'district' or 'area.'
辶 (to walk) — 道 relates to a path or road one walks along.
首 (shǒu) is the historical phonetic element; its modern reading no longer resembles dào, a reminder that sound components can drift after thousands of years of pronunciation change.
日 (sun/day) — relates to 时's meaning of 'time, season'; the phonetic part of the character was later replaced by 寸 in the simplified form
月 (moon) — 期 relates to time measured by the moon's cycles, like a period or term.
其 (qí) gives a hint of the sound — 期 is pronounced qī, a connection that has shifted slightly in tone.
八 here depicts something splitting apart or being divided.
厶 is an old form meaning 'private' or 'one's own' — 公 shows dividing up private property to share it fairly, giving rise to the meaning 'public' or 'fair.'
八 (a hand shape) — one of two hands shown reaching toward the same object.
廾 (two hands together) — jointly holding up one object, giving 共 its meaning 'together, joint, common.'
牛 (ox/cattle) — cattle were among the earliest and most valuable kinds of property, connecting 物 to the general idea of 'object' or 'thing.'
勿 (wù) gives the sound — 物 is also pronounced wù, an exact match.
贝 (shell, an ancient form of currency) — 质 originally meant 'pledge, hostage,' something valuable given as a guarantee, extended to 'quality, substance, nature.'
十 (shí) served as the phonetic base; its pronunciation has since drifted well away from zhì.

meanings: to repeat from mouth to mouth

components.note: 亻 (person) — relates to 传's meaning 'to pass on, transmit,' something passed from person to person.
专 (zhuān) gives a sound hint — 传 is pronounced chuán, sharing the same rhyme though the initial consonant differs.
讠 (speech radical) — shows 说 relates to talking or language
兑 (duì) is the phonetic component; historically 说 was also pronounced closer to 兑's sound before shifting to shuō
身 — depicts a drawn bow
寸 — a hand releasing the arrow
手 (hand) — in the traditional form 擊, 手 contributed the meaning of striking with force, the source of 击's meaning 'to hit, strike.'
卩 (a kneeling figure) — a hungry person kneeling down, about to eat.
皀 (a bowl of food) — the meal in front of them, giving 即 its sense of imminent action, 'right away, that is to say.'
目 (eye) — 眼 refers directly to the eye itself.
艮 (gèn) gives a sound hint — 眼 is pronounced yǎn; the rhyme has drifted apart over the centuries.
钅 (metal) — early mirrors were made of polished bronze.
竟 (jìng) is an exact match for the sound of 镜.
心 (heart) — 愿 relates to a heartfelt wish or desire
原 (yuán) gives a loose sound connection to 愿's reading yuàn
Depicts a person standing tall, gazing up at the moon 月 — the image of looking into the distance, the source of 望's meaning 'to gaze, hope, expect.'
尸, here a variant of 厂, depicts a roof or shelter.
至 depicts arriving or coming to rest — settling under a roof gave 屋 its meaning 'house, room.'
页 (head) — 顶 names the top of the head, the crown.
丁 (dīng) gives the sound — an exact match with 顶.
走 (to walk/run) — 起 relates to standing up and setting into motion.
己 (jǐ) gives a close sound cue — 起 is pronounced qǐ, sharing the same final sound.
广 (shelter) suggests a piece of furniture kept indoors.
木 (wood) — early beds were built from wood, giving 床 its meaning.
兔 depicts a rabbit's body with long ears and a short tail, seen in profile.
